question: The sky appears blue on a clear day, but the light received from the Sun directly is not blue. Explain this observation using scattering of sunlight.

options.A: Air molecules scatter shorter wavelengths more strongly. Blue light is scattered in many directions and reaches the eye from all parts of the sky, so the sky appears blue; direct sunlight still contains many colours and is not blue.
options.B: The sky appears blue because blue light is refracted the most by the atmosphere, while direct sunlight is not refracted.
options.C: The sky appears blue because red light is scattered more strongly than blue light.
options.D: Direct sunlight is blue, but the atmosphere absorbs all blue light except the part seen from the sky.
